definition.title: Edge Types
definition.para: Let C and D be nodes of the subclassical graph. An edge from C to D is a labelled pair (C, D, τ) where the label τ belongs to the set {extension, embedding, equivalence, duality}, with meanings as follows.

listitem.para: Extension. D extends C: every rule of C is a rule of D, and D adds at least one rule not present in C. Extension is the subclassical analogue of the set-inclusion order on theories: Th(C) ⊆ Th(D).

Embedding. C embeds into D via a definitional translation t: there exists a systematic mapping of the connectives of C into complex formulas of D such that C ⊢ φ if and only if D ⊢ t(φ) for all formulas φ.
Equivalence. C and D are equiprovable: each embeds into the other, and the embeddings are mutually inverse up to provable equivalence of the translations.
Duality. D is a structural dual of C: D is obtained from C by a systematic exchange of the roles of premiss and conclusion in one or more families of inference rules, as specified in .
